rows.summary: Payment finality: the base's pay-dem rule (DACS-4 §9.5.9) returns success when a transfer reaches the terminal `included` state, and says that a transfer reaching terminal `failed` did not settle and is a `permanent` failure. The inspected node source labels stored transfers `included` without checking execution; its comment says execution failures are not recorded and surface as `unknown`. This source inference does not establish that a failed transfer is reported as `included` by the deployment, whose executable bytes are unqualified. `included` alone does not independently prove execution. At this branch's base the buyer rail accepts an included status without checking execution; a failed transfer reported as included would be returned as a successful payment (a false success). This current-behaviour finding covers only the buyer rail; a composition review must separately check the seller observer's treatment of failed execution. Current `next` also requires an authenticated Demos BFT proof that Demos cannot supply yet.
rows.tp1: Intended behaviour, pending a separate SDK change that is not on this branch, and composition qualification: TP-1 counts a payment only on an executed record bound to the transfer, never on `included` alone. That is stricter than reading the base's `included` rule literally against the testnet's status wording, and follows the base's statement that a failed transfer did not settle. Current behaviour: at this branch's base, if a transfer whose execution failed is reported as `included`, it is returned as success by the buyer rail, and nothing on this branch prevents it. This statement covers only the buyer rail; the seller observer's treatment of failed execution remains not checked, for composition qualification. A change to the Standard's own pay-dem rule is being proposed separately through the Standard's own process; it is not a condition of TP-1.
rows.label: Intended, pending the SDK's executed-payment check and composition qualification: "Payment executed on Demos testnet; BFT finality not independently proven". Until that check lands, this label would also appear on a failed payment reported as included
rows.closedBy: for the executed-record rule, the SDK's executed-payment check; for finality, Demos executed-status and BFT finality proof APIs, then the Standard's Demos payment-finality binding, then SDK support for finality-bound pay-dem evidence
rows.blocksPublicationNote: Blocks until the SDK's executed-record check and an effect-path test prove that a failed transfer reported as included is not counted as paid. The remaining BFT finality gap is a non-blocking follow-up.

rows.summary: A failed pay-dem transfer reported as `included` would be returned as success, and a definitive failure is not classed `permanent`. DACS-4 §9.5.9 says a transfer that reaches terminal `failed` did not settle and classes it `permanent`. At this branch's base, if a transfer whose execution failed is reported as `included`, it is returned as success (L2: a false success), so the purchase proceeds as if paid. Once a separate SDK change makes such a transfer not ok, SettleResult still carries no failure class and the settlement runner refuses terminal failure evidence for any not-ok result that carries a transaction hash, so the SDK will hold the transfer as unresolved rather than record it as `permanent`.
rows.tp1: Intended behaviour, pending the separate SDK change (see L2) and composition qualification: the SDK holds an executed-but-failed transfer as unresolved, broadcasts nothing a second time, and keeps the purchase settling. That fails closed: the failed transfer is never counted as settled or sent again. It is not the base's `permanent` classification, and TP-1 does not present it as an implemented protection until an effect-path test proves it. Current behaviour at this branch's base: a failed transfer reported as `included` is returned as success.
rows.label: Intended, pending the SDK's executed-payment check and composition qualification: "Payment failed on Demos testnet · purchase held as unresolved; the payment is not sent again". Until then a failed payment reported as included is counted as paid and this label is not shown
rows.closedBy: the SDK's executed-payment check and an effect-path test of the hold; then a failure class on settlement results, so that a definitive failed pay-dem transfer is recorded as `permanent`
rows.blocksPublicationNote: Blocks until the SDK's executed-record check and an effect-path test prove that the failed purchase stays unresolved and the payment is not sent again. The remaining permanent failure classification gap is a non-blocking follow-up.
